But the truth of the matter was that those microfilms were copies of documents forged on an old Woodstock typewriter that had been specially constructed to resemble—to have the same_ peculiarities as—the typewriter that had actually belonged to Alger Hiss' s wife, Priscilla.

Then Whittaker Chambers hid these "old" 1938 microfilms inside a pumpkin on his pumpkin farm. The trouble was, the Eastman Kodak people stated that the type of film we used was not manufactured by their company until 1945.

To this day, whenever the comic strip Peanuts mentions that bird named Woodstock or the mysterious "pumpkin papers," | suspect Charles Schulz is trying to remind me of something.
